hiddenArtifacts.storyUnlocked: Why did All Saints move from May 13 to **November 1**?! Around **731–741 AD**, **Pope St. Gregory III** built a radiant new chapel inside Old **St. Peter’s Basilica** dedicated to *"the Savior, His Mother, all the Apostles, Martyrs, Confessors, and ALL the just made perfect throughout the whole world"*—and consecrated it on **November 1!** A century later in **835**, **Pope Gregory IV** and Emperor Louis the Pious extended **November 1** across all of Europe—turning the golden harvest evening beforehand into ***"All Hallows’ Eve"*** (*Halloween*)!

stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: Standing beneath the surviving towering **Clock Tower of Cluny Abbey** in sunny Burgundy, remember how one French abbot’s compassionate heart gave the whole world a sacred annual day to say **"You are NEVER forgotten!"**
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: Within just a few decades, St. Odilo’s November 2 remembrance proved so deeply healing that **Rome and the entire Universal Church** joyfully adopted **All Souls’ Day** worldwide!

hiddenArtifacts.storyUnlocked: Wait—how did **November 2** become the world’s tenderest day of remembrance?! Right on the eve of the year 1000—in **998 AD**—compassionate **Abbot St. Odilo of Cluny** in Burgundy realized that right after celebrating the radiant saints in heaven on November 1, human hearts ache to remember **every ordinary loved one**—parents, friends, soldiers, strangers with nobody left to visit their graves! So Odilo decreed that every single monastery in Cluny’s vast European network would ring bells, offer Masses, and feed the poor in loving memory of **ALL the faithful departed every November 2!**

stops.eraLabel: 2nd – 4th Century AD · Via Salaria, Rome, Italy
stops.imageCaption: Hushed ancient underground Roman stone archway softly lit by golden oil lamps revealing an early fresco of the Good Shepherd carrying a gentle lamb across His shoulders.
stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: Exploring the quiet underground corridors of Rome’s **Catacomb of Priscilla**—home to the oldest known painting of **Mary holding baby Jesus** (2nd century!)—reminds us that love NEVER ends at the grave!
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: In 2nd-century **2 Maccabees 12:46** and early Roman catacomb prayers alike, praying for departed friends has always been called *"a holy and wholesome thought"*—the ultimate bond of family love that crosses death itself!
stops.saintQuote: Love is stronger than death—those we hold in prayer are never truly lost.

Instead of gloomy epitaphs, they painted **peacocks (symbols of immortality), anchors of hope, and the smiling Good Shepherd** carrying a sheep home on His shoulders, carving tender prayers straight into the stone: ***"In pace!"*** (*"In peace!"*) and ***"May God refresh your spirit in light!"***

stops.ancientPlaceName: Monastero di San Gregorio al Celio & Global Remembrance
stops.imageCaption: Breathtaking twilight hillside glowing with thousands of warm golden flickering candles and vibrant amber marigold petals honoring beloved family members across the world.
stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: Even on **All Souls’ Day**, Catholic priests are uniquely permitted to celebrate **three separate Masses**—one for their parish, one for a personal intention, and one for **every forgotten soul who has no one else to pray for them!**
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: That tender custom of offering three Masses on November 2 began in **15th-century Spain** and was extended to the whole world by **Pope Benedict XV in 1915** right in the midst of World War I’s immense grief!
stops.saintQuote: May the souls of all the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

stops.title: Side-by-Side Courage in the Arena (304 AD)

stops.imageCaption: Golden afternoon sunlight piercing an ancient Roman stone archway in Bologna where two calm steadfast friends encourage one another with peaceful courage.
stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: Near Bologna’s historic **Via San Vitale** (named right after the faithful servant!), the ancient Church of **Santi Vitale e Agricola in Arena** still marks the traditional arena ground of their witness!
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: St. Ambrose recorded that even the Roman executioners hesitated to strike kindhearted Agricola because **everyone in Bologna liked him**—yet Agricola refused to save his skin by denying his friend Vitalis or his Lord!
stops.saintQuote: Do not fear—stand firm beside me, brother, for heaven’s gates stand open!
